newsitem.title: USA: US calls Iraqi request on UN monitors "ludicrous".
newsitem.headline: US calls Iraqi request on UN monitors "ludicrous".

text.p: The Clinton administration Tuesday called "ludicrous" an Iraqi request to approve United Nations staff who would be in charge of distributing humanitarian supplies in northern Iraq.

"If that's not a ludicrous demand by a government that's not in a position to make such a ludicrous demand, then we haven't seen such demands in the past," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
He said Washington wanted to go ahead with the United Nations plan allowing Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food and medicine, but Iraq was hindering operations.
"Iraq is making it very difficult for us to go forward," Burns said at a news briefing.

Last week, the United Nations said the main remaining obstacles concerned the safety and free movement of U.N. personnel and employees of non-governmental organizations in the north amid conflict among Kurdish factions, and Iraq's call for new local U.N. staff.

"And, frankly, I'm surprised that (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein is causing so many problems in trying to work out an effective implementation plan for UN Resolution 986," Burns said, referring to the oil-for-food agreement.
